title: Forward-mode automatic differentiation
outcome: Differentiate supported numerical functions and validate derivatives while preserving the numeric representation carried by dual numbers.
key_terms: A forward-mode automatic differentiation package that evaluates ordinary Julia code with dual numbers.
A number carrying a value and derivative parts, so ordinary arithmetic propagates exact derivatives.
The vector of partial derivatives of a scalar function, returned by `ForwardDiff.gradient`.
The matrix of partial derivatives of a vector-valued function, with one row per output and one column per input.
Buffers created with `similar` on the input so dual numbers fit, unlike a hard-coded `Float64` buffer that blocks differentiation.
approach: Check every automatic derivative against an independent calculation and its shape. `quadratic(x) = x[1]^2 + 3x[2]^2` has gradient `[2x1, 6x2]`, `vector_function` has a 2 by 2 Jacobian, and `generic_storage` uses `similar(x)` so dual numbers can pass through, while `hardcoded_storage` forces `Float64`.

exercises.title: Differentiate analytically
exercises.task: Compute the gradient of x1 squared plus 3x2 squared at `[2, 3]`.
exercises.answer: An analytic case provides an independent reference for the AD implementation.
exercises.why: At `[2, 3]`, 2 times 2 is 4 and 6 times 3 is 18, so the gradient is `[4, 18]`.
exercises.wrong: Testing the gradient only against another AD call reproduces any mistake in the function definition.
exercises.verify: Example A asserts `ForwardDiff.gradient(quadratic, x) ≈ [4, 18]` and a central finite difference along `[1, -1]` matching `dot([4, 18], direction)`.

exercises.title: Check Jacobian axes
exercises.expected: Rows correspond to outputs and columns to inputs.
exercises.answer: A transposed derivative array can have plausible values but the wrong meaning.
exercises.why: Row 1 is the derivative of `x1^2 + x2`, giving `[4, 1]`, and row 2 is the derivative of `x1 * x2`, giving `[3, 2]`.
exercises.wrong: Transposing the Jacobian produces `[4 3; 1 2]`, which has plausible numbers but swaps outputs with inputs.
exercises.verify: Example A asserts `ForwardDiff.jacobian(vector_function, x) ≈ [4 1; 3 2]`; the reference checks its size is `(2, 2)`.

exercises.title: Preserve numeric types
exercises.task: Replace a hardcoded Float64 buffer with `similar(x)`.
exercises.expected: The dual-number path can retain derivative information.
exercises.hint: Use the input representation when the contract is generic.
exercises.answer: Ordinary evaluation alone does not reveal a differentiation-incompatible conversion.
exercises.why: `similar(x)` allocates storage with the input's element type, so dual numbers fit and the gradient `[4, 6]` is returned.
exercises.wrong: Keeping `zeros(Float64, length(x))` works for plain evaluation but cannot store a dual number, so differentiation fails.
exercises.verify: Example B asserts `@test_throws MethodError ForwardDiff.gradient(hardcoded_storage, x)` and the generic gradient `[4, 6]`.

exercises.title: Compare reductions
exercises.task: Differentiate a sum and a mean of two inputs.
exercises.hint: The denominator is part of the objective.
exercises.answer: A reduction change alters gradient scale and cannot be treated as a cosmetic refactor.
exercises.why: Each input contributes once to a sum, giving `[1, 1]`, while dividing by `length(x) = 2` halves that to `[0.5, 0.5]`.
exercises.wrong: Switching a loss from sum to mean without adjusting the learning rate halves every step and changes training behavior.
exercises.verify: The reference asserts both gradients at `[1.0, 2.0]`.

exercises.title: Inspect a branch boundary
exercises.task: Evaluate a nonsmooth function near its kink.
exercises.expected: A library result needs a differentiability interpretation.
exercises.hint: The executed branch is not a symbolic proof.
exercises.answer: At a nondifferentiable point, a returned convention should not be promoted to a unique mathematical derivative.
exercises.why: At the kink of `abs` at 0, ForwardDiff follows whichever branch the code executes and returns that branch's slope.
exercises.wrong: Reporting that value as the derivative of `abs` at 0 claims a unique derivative where only a subgradient set exists.
exercises.verify: Evaluate the derivative just left and right of 0 and state the convention the library used at 0 itself.

exercises.title: Validate a new gradient
exercises.task: Compare analytic or finite-difference directional behavior at several valid inputs.
exercises.expected: Use meaningful tolerances and retain failures.
exercises.hint: Separate approximation error from a wrong formula.
exercises.answer: Derivative checks should inspect shapes, scales and domain assumptions before optimization.
exercises.why: A directional finite difference with a small step approximates the derivative up to truncation and rounding error.
exercises.wrong: Shrinking the step toward 1e-15 to tighten the check lets cancellation error dominate and makes a correct gradient look wrong.
exercises.verify: Compare at several inputs with a stated tolerance, as example A does with `atol = 1e-8`, and keep any failing input.
